result:
All three fixes are in, and the existing suite passes (616 tests). I didn't add a test for the on/off toggle or the rejection, so those paths haven't been run directly.

- **Switching an override off:** the repository's `updateOrg` used to union the new override list with the stored one, so nothing was ever removed. A patch that names `enabledFlagOverrides` now replaces the set, and one that omits it leaves the stored set alone. `toggleFlag` already sends the full set, so only the flag being toggled changes and switching it on again works. The change is in `src/server/repositories/organization-repository.ts`.
- **Settings patches keeping defaults:** `updateOrganizationSchema` in `src/schemas/organization.ts` filled in defaults for every omitted setting. With replace semantics, any unrelated settings update would then have wiped the overrides. The patch schema no longer applies defaults, so an omitted setting stays as stored.
- **Rejecting non-overridable features:** `toggleFlag` in `src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts` now throws when you try to switch on any flag that isn't overridable. Before, it let plan-gated flags like `webhooks` through. Switching such a flag off is still allowed, so a stale override can be cleared. The server action in `src/actions/flags/toggle-flag.ts` no longer skips this check when the plan already enables the flag.
- **Stored overrides on non-overridable flags:** `isEnabled` in `src/lib/feature-flags.ts` now honors an override only when the flag is overridable. Otherwise the flag's own rule (plan, role and so on) decides. That also covers the `webhooks` check in `webhook-service.ts` and the client snapshot, since both go through `isEnabled`.
